root.label: Constructors & Init Order
root.note: Object construction and destruction follow fixed declaration-order phases regardless of initializer list order.

children.label: Strict Subobject Sequence
children.note: Every non-delegating constructor assembles subobjects in four rigid standard-mandated phases.

children.label: 1. Virtual bases first
children.note: The most-derived class initializes all virtual bases once depth-first left-to-right.

children.label: 2. Direct bases left-to-right
children.note: Non-virtual direct base classes construct in the order listed on the class header.

children.label: 3. Members in declaration order
children.note: Non-static data members initialize top-to-bottom as declared in the class body.

children.label: 4. Constructor body runs last
children.note: The compound statement executes only after every base and member has been constructed.

children.label: Mem-Initializer Rules
children.note: Member initializer lists supply construction arguments without altering initialization order.

children.label: Initializer order is ignored
children.note: Reordering members in a colon list still runs them in declaration order, risking uninitialized reads.

children.label: Init beats body assignment
children.note: Initializing members directly avoids default-constructing then reassigning and handles const or ref fields.

children.label: Default member initializers
children.note: Inline member initializers serve as fallbacks skipped whenever a mem-initializer names that member.

children.label: Destruction & Exceptions
children.note: Teardown mirrors construction in reverse and handles partially built or delegated objects carefully.

children.label: Exact reverse teardown
children.note: Destructors run their body first, then members, direct bases, and virtual bases in reverse.

children.label: Partial build unwinds subobjects
children.note: Throwing in a non-delegating constructor destroys built subobjects without calling ~Class().

children.label: Delegating completes lifetime
children.note: Once a target constructor finishes, throwing in the delegating body invokes ~Class().

children.label: Virtual Dispatch Hazard
children.note: Polymorphic dispatch treats the object under construction or destruction as its current class.

children.label: Dynamic type is current class
children.note: Virtual calls inside Base::Base() resolve to Base overriders, never Derived.

children.label: Pure virtual call is UB
children.note: Invoking an unimplemented pure virtual during construction or destruction causes undefined behavior.

children.label: Special & Aggregate Rules
children.note: Constructor declarations govern implicit conversions, default generation, and C++20 aggregate eligibility.

children.label: explicit stops silent conversions
children.note: Use explicit and C++20 explicit(bool) to prevent unwanted scalar or braced conversions.

children.label: User ctor drops default
children.note: Declaring any custom constructor suppresses the implicitly generated default constructor.

children.label: C++20 aggregate restriction
children.note: Any user-declared constructor, even = default, disqualifies a type from aggregate initialization.
